The Gorgeous Tasman Might Be the Family Tiny Home You’ve Been Dreaming Of
29 photos
Photo: Artisan Tiny Homes/Instagram
Even if you think you’ve seen all the dual-loft tiny homes out there, I promise you that The Tasman will surprise and delight you – this gorgeous home on wheels built in the equally-beautiful land of Tasmania, is meant to grow seamlessly from a couple’s elegant cocoon to a cozy haven for their young family.
Just as its name suggests, Artisan Tiny Homes is a brand where tiny living enthusiasts can find the impeccable craftsmanship, attention to detail, and exquisite customization that other mobile homes on the market lack. It’s safe to say that each of the approximately 35 tiny homes built here in almost a decade of activity is a work of art on wheels, sophisticated down to the smallest details and simply oozing personality.
The Tasman is no exception. Purpose-built for a young couple thinking about starting a family in the near future, this compact abode is meant to adapt to the growing needs of a family without major modifications. The solution sounds simple: a dual-loft layout, but the way it was actually envisioned and implemented is much more ingenious and with stunning results, compared to a basic, cookie-cutter version.
What you would typically see in a compact tiny house are two plain, open lofts placed at opposite ends of the layout, and accessed via separate staircases or ladders; these lofts are usually built with cheap materials, and have nothing more than a basic floor and a bed. It’s easy to see why many people shopping for a tiny house tend to avoid dual-loft designs, despite the advantage of having two extra rooms with the same compact footprint.
Photo: Artisan Tiny Homes This is where The Tasman takes a sharp turn to create two of the most beautiful, luxurious loft bedrooms you’ve ever seen. When stepping inside The Tasman, you are welcomed into a spacious open lounge, with high ceilings and no loft above it. A U-shaped kitchen occupies the middle section, alongside an elegant corridor that leads to the bathroom at the other end. The entire loft floor is built above this half of the layout, and accessed via a hidden staircase.
One of the major advantages of this unusual configuration is that both lofts are fully enclosed and, therefore, private. In many ways, they resemble conventional upstairs bedrooms, and this is one of them. The staircase is also unusual, and very practical in terms of space efficiency. It’s a split staircase, meaning that a shared base spreads into different staircases that lead to each bedroom, but it’s cleverly hidden next to the kitchen area.
Both the staircase and the two bedrooms are solidly built with high-quality materials, and it shows – even folks who fear the discomfort and potential safety risks of accessing loft bedrooms will feel perfectly comfortable using this split staircase and accessing both of these rooms on a daily basis. VJ lining boards throughout, waterproof laminate flooring, and large windows further elevate the quality of these lofts.
The main bedroom features a super-comfy walk-around bed, flanked by large windows. The best part? It even features a full-size, floor-to-ceiling wardrobe with more than enough room for the personal items of two people, which is something you rarely find in a tiny house bedroom. The wall with custom-built shutters is visible from the downstairs lounge, and you can see that the bedroom itself is fully private.
Photo: Artisan Tiny Homes The second bedroom is seen more as a multi-purpose space that can evolve as the family grows. Until the first baby is born, the owners can use it a guest room or a hobby/office room. Then, it can be turned seamlessly into an adorable nursery, and then again into a child’s bedroom. The floor space is generous enough for a beautiful baby cradle, and a single bed later on, while large windows (one on each side) fill it with natural light.
The Tasman’s kitchen is also envisioned as a family space. The U-shaped design incorporates generous cupboard space, including a full-height pantry and a dedicated fridge tower. High-quality, full-size appliances are also seamlessly incorporated, and there’s still a generous counter surface left for preparing meals. The outer edge at one end is oversized, in order to double as a breakfast for the whole family – informal and space-efficient.
Even the bathroom is a beautiful space with its own personality. It’s big enough to house a full-size, modern shower cabin, a vintage-style vanity, and a toilet (which is a composting version, for that added touch of sustainability). The blue-and-white checkerboard tiles truly bring this bathroom to life, and the inset shelves inside the shower cabin are another modern touch.
Last, but certainly not least, The Tasman’s lounge is an inviting, warm oasis for the whole family (plus guests). Furniture is kept to a minimum, with just a custom-crafted, elegant sofa that hides storage underneath, and an adorable wood-burning stove that makes the ambiance even cozier. The uninterrupted, generous ceiling height is what makes this lounge feel superbly comfortable, with natural light coming through the glazed main entrance and two windows.
Photo: Artisan Tiny Homes Style-wise, The Tasman exudes the timeless elegance of a modern classic. White VJ walls throughout create that familiar farmhouse aesthetic, beautifully complemented by the darker flooring and natural timber countertops in the kitchen. The buttery shade of the cabinetry in both the kitchen and the bathroom adds a subtle vintage touch, matching the hardware and the large, farmhouse-style sinks.
Lighting also combined modern LED options with romantic hanging light fixtures and chandeliers. Large windows in every room keep this entire tiny house bathed in natural light, which makes its smart layout feel even more spacious.
Judging by this gorgeous interior, you would think that The Tasman must be an XL home on wheels, but its compact footprint doesn’t exceed 8 meters in length (27.8 feet), 2.4 meters (7.8 feet) in width, and 4.3 meters (14 feet) in height. In the words of its own builder, what matters most is not a big house, but one that is cleverly designed.
The gorgeous Tasman starts out as a fully functional, elegant tiny house for a couple, and is ready to morph into a family tiny home over time, once their first baby is born. The Tasman’s dual-loft layout offers much more than the flexibility of a spare bedroom; it creates the privacy, luminosity, storage, and comfort that differentiate real bedrooms from basic loft spaces. This is the kind of tiny home that can truly be loved and enjoyed for generations.
Photo: Artisan Tiny Homes With tiny homes like this beautiful Tasmanian custom-build, downsizing can become a first option, not a second thought. Wonderful craftsmanship, high-quality materials, and a well-planned layout can make the difference between a simple house on wheels and a true home. And let’s not forget beauty – a forever tiny home must look and feel beautiful, and this is where Artisan Tiny Homes truly excels.
Kerrie, and artist and interior designer, is the one who brings these lovely tiny homes to life as if she had a magic wand, together with her husband Kevin, a builder and a restorer, and their daughter who is also a carpenter. Who better than this talented family to know what a family needs in a tiny house? The Tasman is just one of their many custom creations that make dreams come true.

Editor's note: The tiny house exterior photo is for illustration purposes only, all the tiny house interior photos showcase The Tasman
